title: WPSS/2191/2015 of Praveen Kumar Manwal Vs National Institute Of Technology AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2191 of 2015
Praveen Kumar Manwal ... Petitioner
Vs
National Institute of Technology
& another ... Respondents
Mr. V.K. Kaparwan and Ms. Khushboo Chaurasia Advocates, present for the
petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Advocate, present for the respondents.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. While the petitioner was working as a Receptionist
in a Hotel in Rishikesh, namely, Ganga View Hotel in the
year 2007, there was a Police raid in the Hotel premises and
some of the guests in a particular room were found
"gambling". The present petitioner being the "occupier" of the
Hotel was also charged under Section 3/4 of the Gambling
Act along with the guests. Later on the Police filed a charge-sheet in the matter. The matter was pending before the court
of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh,
District Dehradun. The maximum punishment under
Section 3 of the Gambling Act is three months of
imprisonment or a fine not exceeding Rs.200/- and under
Section 4 of the Gambling Act imprisonment not exceeding
one month or fine not exceeding Rs.100/-. This matter,
however, has remained pending before the learned
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate for all these years.
2. Later in the year 2014, an advertisement was
published by National Institute of Technology, Srinagar,
District Pauri Garhwal (from hereinafter referred to as
"Institute") for the post of Superintendent. The advertisement
was published in the month of July 2014. The last date of
submission of application form was 17.09.2014 where the
petitioner admittedly applied for the post of Superintendent.
The petitioner appeared in the written examination on
14.10.2014 and on the next date i.e. 15.10.2014 viva

2
voce/interview was held. Subsequently, the petitioner was
declared successful and was given appointment letter on
11.08.2015. The appointment letter stated as under:-
"I am delighted to inform you that your name has
been recommended for the appointment to the
post of Superintendent in this Institute. I am
confident, you will be happy to work with this
Institute which is located in Himalayan State. The
Office Order to that effect along with the terms
and conditions governing your appointment is
enclosed.
The appointment is effective from the date of
joining the post. Please communicate your
acceptance to the undersigned within 05 days
from the date of issue of this letter and join the
Institute on or before 24th August, 2015. You shall
first report to the Establishment Section along
with duly filled in attestation form, all original
certificates for verification of the documents &
completing other formalities essential for
appointment at this Institute."
3. It is again an admitted case of the respondents
that though the petitioner did not join on the post of
Superintendent, but he has informed the Assistant Registrar
(Administration) of the Institute telephonically on
13.08.2015, a fact which is admitted by the respondents,
that there is a criminal case pending against him under the
Gambling Act in which the decision is likely to be given soon
by the court concerned, and only thereafter the petitioner
would be in a position to join on the said post. The criminal
case has already been referred in the preceding paragraphs.
4. The Institute vide its letter dated 24.08.2015
informed the petitioner that the last date to join the post of
Superintendent is extended up to 23.09.2015 and in case
the petitioner fails to join the said post, the appointment
letter will be treated as cancelled. Thereafter, the petitioner
moved a representation on 22.09.2015 before the concerned
authority stating that a criminal case is pending against

3
him, in which he has been falsely implicated. He has further
stated that there is no evidence against him and further
sought extension of time to join on the post of
Superintendent. On the said representation, the Institute
vide letter dated 05.10.2015 as a last opportunity he was
granted time to join the Institute on or before 19.10.2015
with a rider that he must submit a clearance regarding the
criminal case pending against him at the time of joining.
5. Since the sole difficulty with the petitioner was the
criminal case pending against him, he therefore invoked the
inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of
Cr.P.C., and filed a petition before this Court.
6. The application filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.,
was disposed of by the learned Single Judge of this Court
vide order dated 06.11.2015, which reads as under:-

"Ms. Khushboo Chaurasia, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Hariom Bhakuni, A.G.A. for the State.
Ms. Khushboo Chaurasia, learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner, submits that petitioner is
facing trial before the Judicial Magistrate, Rishikesh under
Section 3/4 of Public Gambling Act. Since, petitioner has
been offered Government job, therefore, pendency of the
criminal case may be a ground to decline him to give
joining. Therefore, petitioner shall confess the guilt before
the Trial Court by moving confession application. She
further contends that since maximum punishment is less
than one year for the offence punishable under Section 3/4
of Public Gambling Act, therefore, in the light of
judgment rendered in the case of Devi Sharma and
another Vs. State of Uttarakhand reported in 2015 (1)
NCC 363, petitioner should be released on probation after
admonition of the punishment, so that confession may not
be treated as disqualification as provided under Section 12
of the Probation of Offenders Act.
Mr. Hariom Bhakuni, learned A.G.A. for the State,
has no serious objection to the suggestions made by Ms.
Khushboo Chaurasia, learned counsel for the petitioner.

4
Present petition, thus, stands disposed of with the
aforesaid liberty to the petitioner to approach the Trial
Magistrate.
CRMA No. 1910 of 2015 also stands disposed of
accordingly."
7. The petitioner subsequently moved an application
before the trial court confessing his guilt under the
provisions of Gambling Act and pleaded that he may also be
given benefit of Section 3 & 4 of the Probation of Offenders
Act and be released under the said Act. Since the petitioner
pleaded guilty, the learned Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Rishikesh invoking his powers under Section
252 of Cr.P.C., convicted him but instead of imposing any
sentence he was released under the Probation of Offenders
Act.
8. The petitioner in the present petition claims the
benefit of Section 12 of the Probation of Offenders Act, which
reads as under:-
"Section 12. Removal of disqualification attaching
to conviction. - Notwithstanding anything contained
in any other law, a person found guilty of an offence
and dealt with under the provisions of Section 3 of
Section 4 shall not suffer disqualification, if any,
attaching to a conviction of an offence under such law :
 Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to
a person who, after his release under section 4, is
subsequently sentenced for the original offence."
9. Since the petitioner has been released under
Probation of Offenders Act, disqualification presently
attached to the conviction of the present petitioner, as
regarding his appointment as Superintendent in the
Institute goes away and the benefit of Section 12 of the
Probation of Offenders Act has to be given to the petitioner.
10. Even though the learned counsel for the
respondent Mr. Paresh Tripathi has not been able to place
any provision of law before this Court, which shows that

5
conviction by a criminal court automatically disqualifies a
person from service in the respondent establishment yet
assuming for the sake of argument that there is such a
provision in law which would have disqualified the present
petitioner from appointment in the Institute, the same
disqualification will not come in his way now in view of
Section 12 of the Probation of Offenders Act and a benefit of
which has to be given to the petitioner. The Hon'ble Apex
Court in Divisional Personnel Officer, Southern Railway
Another Vs. T.R. Chellappan reported in (1976) 3 SCC
190 has interpreted the provisions of Section 12 of Probation
of Offenders Act. It has been laid down in the above
judgment that a person who has been granted benefit of
Section 3 or 4 of Probation of Offenders Act "shall not suffer
disqualification, if any, attached to the conviction of an
offence under the law". The Hon'ble Apex Court explained
that the above provision means firstly that there must be a
disqualification resulting from a conviction and secondly
that this disqualification must be provided by some law,
other than Probation of Offenders Act. The benefit which is
given under Section 12 of the Probation of Offenders Act is
that disqualification which results from a conviction will not
apply after the benefit of the Probation of Offenders Act.
These disqualifications are the one such as prescribed under
different statutes for example in Representation of the
People's Act, Company's Act, etc. In the present case
therefore even if there is a disqualification attached to the
appointment of the petitioner, the same is no more a
disqualification in view of Section 12 of Probation of
Offenders Act.
11. The learned counsel for the respondent Mr.
Paresh Tripathi has submitted that the appointment of the
petitioner has not been cancelled or withdrawn as of now.

6
Therefore, in case, the conviction of the present petitioner
was the only disqualification attached to the petitioner for
his job in the Institute, the same would not come in his way
in view of the benefit given under Section 12 of the Probation
of Offenders Act.
12. There is, however, yet another contention of Shri.
Paresh Tripathi who submits that although this will not be a
disqualification, yet the petitioner has not been fair to the
Institute as he did not disclosed the fact that he is facing a
criminal trial and that he was arrested and obtained bail.
13. Learned counsel for the respondent submits that
application form itself asked each of the candidates to
furnish certain information, which reads as under:-
"(a) Proof of Date of Birth (If not attached application will be
rejected).
(b) Category Certificate (For SC/ST/OBC Candidates only) (if
not attached, application will be considered in OPEN).
(c) Non-creamy Layer Certificate (for OBC candidates only,
based on parents income). The Candidates are requested to
submit the non-creamy layer certificate issued on or after 1st
April, 2014. if caste certificate or non-creamy layer is not
attached, the application will be considered in OPEN.
(d) Person with Disability Certificate from Competent
Authority only will be accepted (for PWD candidates only, if
not attached application will be considered in OPEN).
(e) SSC (10th Standard) certificate and marksheet.
(f) HSSC (10 + 2) certificate and marksheet.
(g) ITI certificate indicating duration of course and the trade
(without certificate ITI qualification will not be considered).
(h) Final Year Marksheet/Grade Cards and Diploma/Degree
Certificates for the Examinations mentioned in the
Application Form in the same sequence. (Any degree

7
mentioned with not be considered unless certificates are
attached.)
(i) Experience Certificate from employer (Any experience
claimed without certificate will not be counted).
(j) For the post of Students Activity and Sports Assistant, the
candidates are required to furnish self-attested photocopies
of the certificates indicating the following:
(i) Representation of the college in Inter-University/Inter-Collegiate tournament.
(ii) Participation in Organization of students level activities."
K. Any other information which the candidate wants to
provide (One Page only, duly signed).

14. Learned counsel for the respondents would
emphasis that the condition given in 4k of the form states
that any other information which the candidate wants to
provide, and hence in all fairness the petitioner ought to
have disclosed the fact that there was a criminal case filed
against him and he remained in police custody for three
days and thereafter he was released on bail. The petitioner
has confessed his guilt before the Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Rishikesh is withheld from the Institute.

15. The condition given in item 4K of the
advertisement has been perused. Item no.4 of the "form"
seeks certain particulars, which a candidate has to furnish
in his application form, such as proof of date of birth,
whether he belongs to any reserved category such as SC, ST,
OBC and his non-creamy layer certificate, disability
certificate (if required), Class-X certificate, Class-XII
certificate, final year mark-sheet of diploma experience
certificate, any certificate for students activities etc. Though
in the last at 4k of the advertisement, a general information

8
has been sought such as any other information has to be
read in context to other remaining information which are
sought. This Court has already seen the nature of
information sought from the candidate is primarily essential
particulars, such as date of birth, education qualification
etc. Technically therefore it was not mandatory for the
petitioner to have disclosed the pendency of the criminal
proceeding.
16. Another objection has been raised by the learned
counsel for the respondents that this fact was also not
disclosed by the petitioner during the interview. Though it
may be true that fairness demanded that the petitioner
should have furnished these details to the respondents but
here again petitioner cannot be faulted, inasmuch it is an
admitted case of the respondents that on 13.08.2015 the
petitioner on his own informed the concerned authority
about the pending criminal case against him and prior to it
we find nothing on record to suggest that the respondents
had sought any such details from the petitioner and the fact
that he is facing a criminal trial was informed to the
respondents by the petitioner himself suo motu.
17. Having made the above determination that there
is no disqualification attached to the petitioner, he will be at
liberty to approach the authority concerned along with copy
of this order.
18. The writ petition stands disposed. No order as to
costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
02.12.2015
Nitesh
